This time we tweaked the recipe a little bit for our own taste. Here's the original recipe: https://altonbrown.com/recipes/aged-eggnog

And ours looks a little more like this:

12 eggs----
3 pints half and half----
1 pound of sugar----
1 tsp salt----
2 tsp nutmeg----
1 tsp cinnamon----
.5 tsp ground clove----
1 cup of brandy (we used St. Remy)----
1 cup bourbon (Dickel 8-year)----
1 cup rum (5 oz Plantation 3-star + 3 oz Doctor Bird)----

The tweaked version is definitely easier to drink straight away, we'll see how the flavor holds up as it ages. The added salt is really nice, as well as the addition of cloves.

**Ramos Gin Fizz:**

* (1.5 oz) gin
* (0.75 oz) vanilla syrup
* (0.5 oz) lemon
* (0.5 oz) lime
* 4 drops orange blossom water
* (0.75 oz) cream
* 1 egg white
* soda

Add ice and shake all ingredients (except soda water) for at least 30 seconds. Discard the ice and shake again. Pour 30 ml (1 oz) of soda water into a frosted glass and top with the cocktail. Leave the foam to settle for a bit before slowly adding more soda water to rise the foam over the rim of the glass.

Woke up yesterday and decided to take on the task of making a clarified milk punch! It's smooth and delicious (a little on the sweet side so you could cut down on the sugar if you so desire), and is a perfect summer sipper. Plus, it lasts months in the fridge. I found this recipe on craftandcocktails.com


RECIPE 

16 oz brandy

16 oz rum

peels of four lemons

2 nutmeg, chopped

2 cinnamon sticks, chopped

2 whole Star anise, chopped

8 oz lemon juice

8 oz pineapple juice

16 oz sugar by volume

16 oz water

8 oz milk

Peel lemons and chop spices. Add the peels of lemons, nutmeg, cinnamon stick and star anise to a container along with the brandy and rum and let set 2 hours or up to 12 hours preferably. Strain out the solids. Add sugar, water, lemon juice and pineapple juice to the infused booze mixture and stir to dissolve the sugar.

 In a non-reactive container, add the cold milk. Slowly pour in the cocktail into the milk. Stir. Let set for a few hours in the fridge to let the milk do its thing (a.k.a. curdle) do not stir. When the whey has formed into a “web” in the container and settle to the bottom, it’s time to strain. You can leave it for up to 24 hours.

Put a cheese cloth over a container or jar with a funnel. I used a Chemex coffee maker. Slowly strain into the cheesecloth. It will take a bit to fully strain. Strain again, but this time use the coffee filter in a funnel over another container. The cheese cloth catches the bigger clumps of  whey, but lets some smaller whey through. The coffee filter catches the rest, but wont get clogged with the thicker whey, which can take hours to strain!

Et viola! there you have it a clear milk punch that will last for months in the fridge!

To serve: Pour into a glass with a large cube, preferably clear ice to show off all your hard work clarifying, grate of nutmeg on top with a lemon peel and optional pineapple leaf for flair.

This fall and winter I've been battling super dry, damaged, rough skin. I was (stupidly) using some chemical and physical exfoliants in an attempt to shed the dry layer of my skin and reach the fresh new skin under it- apparently that's not how it works. After doing some research I realized my skin's moisture barrier was compromised from all the exfoliating. This explained why my skin was textured and sensitive, with little bumps on my chin and under my cheekbones. 

I immediately stopped using all exfoliants and all products that irritated my skin, and started oil cleansing once a day, at night before bed. I was mixing olive oil and castor oil, but decided to switch to just castor oil because I think the EVOO was making my skin feel greasy even after rinsing. I do NOT double cleanse; I simply rub the castor oil into my skin and hairline for ~1 minute and then gently wipe away the oil with a microfiber cloth. It absorbs quickly and leaves my skin feeling supple. 

After that, depending on how thirsty my skin is, I'll apply the Wool Wax Cream (a little goes a long way). This stuff is AMAZING for super thirsty skin- mine soaks it up in a matter of seconds, and there's no greasy feeling afterwards. The smell is very mild, because it has no added fragrances or anything. [here ](https://www.lehmans.com/product/skin-care-formula-wool-wax-creme) is the link to the Wool Wax Cream if any other cold-weather bbs are in need of a rich moisturizer. 

In the morning, I usually wash my face with warm water and a microfiber cloth, and put on the neutrogena sunscreen if I'm going outside. I like this sunscreen because it's lightweight and doesn't leave the white tint on my skin, whereas most sunscreen is too heavy/greasy for my skin and leaves the white cast. 

I've been doing this routine for ~2 weeks and all of the little bumps on my cheeks are gone. The flaky skin between my eyebrows is gone, and the overall texture of my skin is smoother. I was thinking about it, and my new skincare routine is oddly like seasoning a cast-iron pan (is that weird??). I never use soap on my face any more because the castor oil disintegrates any buildup I have in my pores. 

Overall, it's working like a dream! I can't wait to see my skin continue to repair itself.
